target_customer: Individuals and businesses (real estate, restaurants, ecommerce, enterprises like DoorDash and Redfin) buying on-demand photography and video
problem: Booking a professional photographer takes advance notice, price negotiation and quality risk. Snappr offers fixed prices, instant booking and vetted photographers, later adding workflows and AI tools.
business_model: Marketplace take rate (20 percent on basic packages in 2017) plus enterprise SaaS and AI tools

founders.name: Matt Schiller
founders.background_notes: From the YC page: web development, pilot, McKinsey alum, UNSW alum, medical doctor. SmartCompany 2017 mentions other co-founders without naming them.

competitors.name: PhotoSesh
competitors.what: US platform matching hosts with photographers for casual events; photographers set 30 to 75 dollar hourly rates, 20 percent commission

competitors.name: Pinpic
competitors.what: Canadian service connecting travelers with local photographers
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; shut down a few months after the article per its update

competitors.name: Perfocal
competitors.what: UK service with automatic matching of clients and photographers, in beta

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, matching and payment marketplace with photo delivery; standard engineering. Later AI image tools raised the bar.

defensibility.rationale: Supply of vetted photographers (about 5 percent acceptance per its site) and enterprise workflows add friction, but demand could multihome.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the niche by search; Snappr grew to a Series A in 2020 and reportedly a Series B in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch Feb 2017 said hiring photographers online often needed advance notice and price negotiation. Snappr launched with 59 to 249 dollar fixed packages and was live in San Francisco, San Jose and Australian cities.

branding.domain_note: Uses snappr.com, an exact .com with the dropped vowel.

identity.visual_style: Clean marketplace and AI tool pages

branding.community_and_virality: Photographer community with peer review vetting; photographers' forum posts call it Uber for photography with mixed enthusiasm.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable short name and wide trade coverage, but sources show no mascot or viral brand moment; confusable with Snapchat results.

pivots.to: Visual content platform with enterprise workflows and AI tools
pivots.why: Not stated by a source I opened; the current site describes workflows and Magic AI tools.

outcome_analysis: Snappr started in Sydney and joined YC in W17 with fixed-price on-demand photography, raising a 2.5 million seed in September 2017 and a 10 million Series A in 2020 led by Basis Set. It grew into enterprise workflows and AI tools for customers such as DoorDash and Redfin and now claims a 250 person team. Marketplace supply depth and enterprise contracts explain steady growth without a large exit.
notes: A 28M Series B led by Foundry in October 2025 (total 42M) appears in search summaries citing Sacra and Axios but I opened neither, so it is not recorded as a round. A pulse2 and PetaPixel total of 13M after the Series A agrees with Crunchbase. Competitor article is dated 2017-06 (updated 2017-12), about five months after the batch start. Total funding after 2020 is therefore unverified, so coverage is partial. Founding year varies: 2016 (Sydney) versus 2017 (San Francisco).
